logos.title: Weinachy
paragraphs: I create concept-driven logos that are clear, confident, and crafted with precision—often using the golden ratio to achieve visual harmony. My focus is on building meaningful, aesthetically clean identities for startups and personal brands.

Over the course of my career, I’ve designed more than 60 logos, each tailored to reflect the essence of the brand. I approach every project with attention to detail, from concept development to full brand identity systems.

The Weinachy logo was developed with a focus on clarity, structure, and distinctiveness. Drawing from the brand’s European roots, I crafted a minimal and modern mark that feels both professional and personal.

Clean lines, balanced proportions, and thoughtful spacing give the logo a confident visual presence, while subtle design choices ensure it stands apart with its own recognizable identity. It seamlessly adapts across digital and print applications, anchoring the brand’s visual language.

The design merges clean geometry with a tech-savvy aesthetic, capturing the brand’s dynamic nature while staying visually simple and adaptable. It’s built to perform across platforms—from product listings to blockchain interfaces—while maintaining a strong, recognizable identity in a fast-moving digital space.

Agora Events, a vibrant music festival, needed a logo that radiated joy, rhythm, and movement. The challenge was to capture the energy of live music and human connection in a single mark.

While exploring visual directions, I came across a maze-like painting that instantly resonated with the spirit of the event. Inspired by its playful complexity, I developed a dynamic and cheerful logo that feels spontaneous yet intentional—just like a great festival experience.

Nami 8 approached me with a unique challenge: to create a 3D logo that would embody the essence of a single drop of water.

Inspired by the fluidity and form of water itself, I designed a custom typeface built entirely from drop-like shapes. The result is a soft, flowing, and sculptural logo that feels organic yet refined—perfectly aligned with the brand’s name and concept.

bannerposter.title: Weinachy
paragraphs: Created for Weinarchy, an Austrian wine e-shop, this banner was designed for their appearance at a wine exhibition in Berlin, Germany. The concept was bold and immersive: one large poster split into five individual pieces, each standing as a visual fragment of a bigger story.My goal was to reflect the brand’s confident, modern voice through dynamic layout and expressive typography—while ensuring each segment worked on its own and as part of the whole.

bannerposter.title: Yoonico
paragraphs: ommissioned from Italy, this series was designed for Yoonico, an innovative NFT e-shop where technology and business intersect. The goal was to reflect that futuristic energy with bold compositions and sleek typography. I created several animated and static banners that captured the brand’s forward-thinking spirit—clean, digital, and visually rich.

bannerposter.title: Font design
paragraphs: This is one of my favorite projects—a celebration of Georgian script through modern design. I created a custom display font by drawing bold, unique shapes for each letter, inspired by the rhythm and character of the Georgian alphabet.Each letter then became the centerpiece of its own poster, transforming typography into powerful visual compositions. The result is a series that feels experimental, local, and deeply personal—bold in both form and cultural identity.

bannerposter.title: The Immortal Legacy
paragraphs: This personal project brings to life the statues of Georgia’s great historical figures through design. Combining authentic modern minimalism with subtle antique and bold elements, I reimagined these iconic sculptures as striking, contemporary visuals. This series is close to my heart—a fusion of heritage and fresh expression that celebrates Georgian culture in a new light.

print-design.title: Gurian Vodka
paragraphs: Family Vodka

This project was a deep visual exploration of a place and its spirit. Gurian Vodka is crafted using a traditional family recipe from Guria, and my task was to reflect that bold regional identity through design.

I drew inspiration from Guria’s vibrant nature, subtropical colors, wave-like geography, and even the forgotten Soviet mosaics of Lanchkhuti. These elements shaped the label’s composition and symbolism—especially the sun-sea motif and mosaic fragments, which I reinterpreted to give new life to disappearing local stories.The bottle’s form and proportions followed the mood of the label itself, resulting in a product that feels both culturally rooted and visually modern.

paragraphs: e-comerce shop

This project was a comprehensive dive into visual consistency across touchpoints. Working with Weinachy, an Austria-based company, I developed a wide range of brand materials to support both their corporate presence and public-facing communication.

From business cards, banners, and invoices to brochures, posters, and large-format Messe exposition graphics—I focused on creating a cohesive visual language that reflected the brand’s tone: professional, approachable, and distinctly European.

print-design.title: Growlab
paragraphs: I create concept-driven logos that are clear, confident, and crafted with precision—often using the golden ratio to achieve visual harmony. My focus is on building meaningful, aesthetically clean identities for startups and personal brands.

Growlab is a modern plant care company focused on sustainable growing solutions. My collaboration with them centered around creating a warm, informative, and approachable visual language for their printed materials.

I designed a variety of assets—including guidebooks, brochures, booklets, business cards, sticker sets, and seed bunk labels—all aimed at supporting Growlab’s mission to make plant care simple and inspiring.
Each item was tailored to reflect their eco-conscious identity, using clean layouts, earthy tones, and playful but instructive graphics to engage both new and seasoned plant lovers.
Meet Mariam Gogichaishvili, a graphic designer who has a passion for creating something out of nothing

I’m Mariam Gogichaishvili, a graphic designer who’s always had the passion to make something from nothing. I was around 13 or 14 when a local poet came to our school—some students read his work, and some of us made little videos. I ended up making videos for all five teams. That was the first time I got curious about design software, and honestly, I’ve been hooked ever since.

Currently, I specialize in branding, logo design, posters, motion graphics, simple 3D objects, custom fonts and forms. I even built my own portfolio website—and discovered I really enjoy web design too. I work both independently and with teams, and I’m most in my element when I’m deep in the creative process, chasing bold ideas and watching them come to life.
